intro.headline: MSc Computer Engineering @ Politecnico di Torino · Human–Computer Interaction
intro.homePrimary: I am an MSc student in Computer Engineering at Politecnico di Torino, specializing in human–computer interaction — how people actually use an interface, and how you measure that honestly. My research has included automated program repair and LLM agents that build and test software without a human in the loop.
intro.homeSecondary: The projects here are hobby work — things I was curious enough about to spend months on. Both apply computer vision to architecture: measuring how building styles relate across time and geography, and what happens to a design manifesto when it meets a climate.
about: I am an MSc student in Computer Engineering at Politecnico di Torino, with a BSc from Bilkent University, specializing in human–computer interaction. My research in software engineering includes a characterisation study of defect benchmarks and evaluation bias in automated program repair, and using LLM agents to automate build and test environment setup for open-source software.

The projects on this site are hobby work — things I was curious enough about to spend months on. Both apply computer vision to architecture: one mapping architectural style similarity across 25 traditions in CLIP latent space, the other measuring how much of Le Corbusier’s Five Points survives being built in a different climate.
